item.title: At Cornell, rape allegations spark outrage, soul-searching over campus culture
item.description: The case has reignited scrutiny of how law enforcement and universities handle sexual assault complaints, with students questioning whether processes are enough to protect them.
item.dc:creator: Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: Cornell University student Sophia Riley Sim skipped classes this week, consumed by allegations in a lawsuit that several members of a fraternity raped a young woman in 2024 and troubled by how her university handled the case. "Cornell has failed our community through its lack of accountability, transparency, and failure to address the state of the Cornell student body at this time," Sim, a junior, said at a public hearing on sexual assault organized by Cornell's Student Assembly on Thursday. "There has been a lack of meaningful communication from university leadership, administrators, and faculty." The Ivy League school has defended its handling of the matter, saying it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi fraternity involved in the alleged assault from campus. The school said it imposed a range of disciplinary measures, including expulsions. It did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment. The hearing, held in one of Cornell's historic halls, came days after the allegations became public with the [USN:L1N45N0UA TEXT:"filing of a civil lawsuit"] and the announcement that a criminal investigation would be reopened. The case has reignited scrutiny of how law enforcement and universities handle sexual assault complaints, with students questioning whether processes are enough to protect them. It has also drawn the attention of New York state officials, who have appointed a special prosecutor to investigate. FEELING UNSAFE At the Assembly hearing, speakers recounted experiences with sexual assault, broke down in tears and criticized the response of the prestigious university. The Student Assembly - which represents Cornell's undergraduate students and can make proposals to the university's bodies or officers - unanimously approved a resolution calling on Cornell administrators to provide a full account of how the investigation was handled. It also asked the university to disclose any disciplinary measures imposed on the accused students, and publish annual reports on the outcomes of any future sexual misconduct cases. Organizers asked that many of the dozens of speakers at the hearing not be identified or recorded. One student said she had worked all her life to be accepted to Cornell and now felt that it had not been worth it. Several others said they did not feel safe on the 2,300-acre campus in New York's Finger Lakes region. Thirty-five percent of undergraduate women reported experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact involving force or incapacitation since entering Cornell, according to a university survey conducted in 2025 and published on its website. That figure was up from 20% in 2021. "WE ARE GOING TO FIGHT" The lawsuit alleges fraternity members supplied the woman with alcohol, marijuana and ketamine before sexually assaulting her after she became incapacitated. It also alleges Cornell failed to adequately punish some of the accused students and allowed some to seek reduced penalties by writing essays. Cornell denied that essays were the only punishment meted out. The New York Times, citing internal Cornell documents, said the men all denied any wrongdoing, with some saying the sex was consensual and others denying participation. Cornell students have scheduled a rally for Monday to call for additional measures to protect victims. Jane Wang, a public policy major, said she had reported a sexual assault to the university and that the process caused additional distress. "In the midst of all of my mental, physical, and emotional recovery from the assault, I was also met with an abundance of paperwork, very little instruction on how to navigate it, and no follow up from our office about an outcome," she said. The Ivy League school said in a statement on its website that it could not provide full information regarding individual students and disciplinary outcomes because of restrictions imposed by privacy laws. "Our adherence to privacy laws should not be interpreted as indifference to the seriousness of the conduct at issue," the statement said. A handful of other female students told the hearing they had been sexually assaulted on Cornell's campus in the past, without sharing details. Saanya Agarwal, Cornell University's student women's issues representative, said the findings of the 2025 survey on sexual assaults were unacceptable. "Clearly, this is an issue our campus and campuses throughout the United States... it's something that we're not going to accept," said Agarwal. "We are going to fight."

item.title: US-Ukrainian investment fund seals first critical minerals deal
item.description: The joint US-Ukrainian reconstruction investment fund has sealed its first critical minerals deal alongside four other new projects, one of its top US officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: The joint US-Ukrainian reconstruction investment fund has sealed its first critical minerals deal alongside four other new projects, one of its top US officials told Reuters. The fund, established as part of the [USN:NP8N3NZ01 TEXT:"minerals pact"] the two countries signed in April last year following a push by US President Donald Trump, is focused on five strategic sectors from minerals and defence to energy and infrastructure. Conor Coleman, head of investments at the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), said the fund's projects now total around $70 million and showed Washington's support for Kyiv in the long-running war with Russia. "It's absolutely imperative for the Ukrainian people that we're investing now," Coleman said in an interview, referring to the ongoing damage to Ukraine as it faces another winter. The long-anticipated first minerals deal will inject roughly $30 million into a "joint investment platform" with BGV Group, a firm founded by Hennadii Butkevych, the billionaire co-owner of Ukraine's largest supermarket chain ATB. Coleman said it would initially focus on early-stage mining projects across Ukraine and target rare earths, uranium, beryllium and zirconium deposits. "They are all on the US critical minerals list, so it ties in very well with what we're looking to do from a (US) administration priority (standpoint)," Coleman said. POWER PROJECTS Two of the other new projects announced on Friday aim to shore up Ukraine's power and heating networks after a rise in Russian attacks on key infrastructure ahead of winter. Coleman said one would add to the near $100 million the DFC has just agreed to lend Ukraine's largest private energy company [USN:L4N4581E1 TEXT:"DTEK"] for a new battery system that will provide backup power to approximately 600,000 Ukrainian homes for up to two hours. The project will also have "access to capital if damages arise". The fund will also take an equity stake in a combined heat and power co-generation platform designed to help build and run off a number of "energy hubs" aimed at restoring damaged electricity and heat supplies to households. Coleman also said the fund was looking for more capital to increase its capacity.

item.title: ＦＲＢ、利上げ・据え置きとも選択肢 物価対応が優先課題＝シカゴ連銀総裁
item.description: [２日 ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２日、９月の雇用統計で労働市場が安定していることが示され...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢ、利上げ・据え置きとも選択肢　物価対応が優先課題＝シカゴ連銀総裁 2:44 配信

８月２７日撮影　 REUTERS/Ann Saphir

[２日 ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２日、９月の雇用統計で労働市場が安定していることが示されたとし、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）にとってインフレへの対応が重要な課題になっていると述べた。

グールズビー氏はＦＯＸビジネス・ネットワークの番組「ザ・ビッグ・マネー」で、ＦＲＢは今月の会合で追加利上げを決定すべきか、それとも利上げを見送るべきかとの質問に対し、利上げと据え置きのいずれについても「なお十分に検討の余地がある」とし、「インフレ率が目標とする２％に向けて再び低下していることを示す証拠がまとまるか見極めたい」と語った。

ＦＲＢは９月１５─１６日に開いたＦＯＭＣで０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定。利上げは２０２３年７月以来３年２カ月ぶりで、決定は全会一致だった。１０月２７─２８日の次回ＦＯＭＣで追加利上げが決定されるとの観測は後退している。

グールズビー総裁は今年のＦＯＭＣで投票権を持っていない。

item.title: Lula diz que brasileiros têm o direito de ter quantos cartões de crédito quiserem
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disse nesta sexta-feira que os brasileiros têm o direito de ter quantos cartões de crédito quiserem, após afirmar na véspera que avaliava a proibição de mais de um cartão por pessoa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disse nesta sexta-feira que os brasileiros têm o direito de ter quantos cartões de crédito quiserem, após afirmar na véspera que avaliava a proibição de mais de um cartão por pessoa. "Ontem falei da preocupação com o cartão de crédito, pois os juros são indecentes", disse Lula em publicação no X. "Cada cidadão tem o direito de ter quantos cartões de crédito quiser." "O que não aceito é que bancos enviem para a casa das pessoas sem que elas tenham solicitado. Vamos acabar com essa prática e com os juros abusivos no Brasil", acrescentou. Em entrevista no Flow Podcast na noite de quinta-feira, o presidente, que tenta a reeleição, disse que está estudando com o Banco Central medidas para [USN:L1N45O01C TEXT:"restringir"] os cartões. "O povo gasta com mais facilidade o cartão de crédito. E ele só vai ver o rombo no final. Nós estamos discutindo com o Banco Central, nós vamos proibir os bancos (de) darem mais que um cartão de crédito para as pessoas", havia dito Lula na entrevista. O Banco Central vem sinalizando que vai adotar medidas macroprudenciais para enfrentar o que vê como um aumento exacerbado do endividamento. Mas limitar os consumidores a um único cartão de crédito nunca esteve em consideração, disse à Reuters uma pessoa a par das discussões. As autoridades econômicas estão estudando práticas adotadas em outros países que tiveram algum sucesso em conter empréstimos abusivos, acrescentou a fonte. "Até onde sabemos, não há nenhum grande mercado no mundo que imponha uma regra rígida de um único cartão por pessoa", escreveram analistas do Jefferies em relatório sobre a declaração de quinta-feira de Lula.

item.title: ＥＣＢ総裁の早期退任観測、明確化必要 伊に後任候補なし＝伊経済相
item.description: [ローマ ２日 ロイター] - イタリアのジョルジェッティ経済・財務相は２日、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁が...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＥＣＢ総裁の早期退任観測、明確化必要　伊に後任候補なし＝伊経済相 2:28 配信

ラガルドECB総裁。7月23日、フランクフルトで撮影。REUTERS/Heiko Becker/File Photo

[ローマ ２日 ロイター] - イタリアのジョルジェッティ経済・財務相は２日、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁が任期途中で辞任する可能性があるといううわさについて、事実関係を明確にする必要があるとの認識を示した。

ジョルジェッティ財務相は「ラガルド総裁が何を考えているのか私には分からないが、この件を明確にしておくことは重要だと考える」と述べた。

また、イタリアは現時点でＥＣＢ総裁の後任候補として推薦する人材はいないと述べた。

ラガルド総裁を巡っては、２０２７年のフランス大統領選への出馬を目指し、ＥＣＢ総裁を任期途中で辞任するとの観測が浮上していた。これに対しラガルド総裁は今週、仏大統領選への出馬は「全く良い考えではない」と述べ、仮にＥＣＢ総裁職を退任するとしても、任期満了より数カ月早い時期にとどまるとの考えを示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：欧州熱波、損害保険未カバーの企業損失が拡大 アングル：トランプ氏がＮＡＴＯ首脳会議で見せた硬軟2つの顔、各国は冷静対応 アングル：トランプ氏賛美から一転、 戦略転換迫られるメローニ氏 アングル：インド「高級水」市場が急成長、富裕層にブーム到来 最終更新: 10/3(土) 2:28 ロイター

item.title: Israeli officials to question co-pilot of flydubai flight, source says
item.description: “It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts,” said flydubai CEO Ghaith Al Ghaith.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Israeli officials to question co-pilot of flydubai flight, source says

“It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts,” said flydubai CEO Ghaith Al Ghaith.

Travellers board a FlyDubai aircraft at Ben Gurion International Airport, in Lod, near Tel Aviv, Israel, Sep 30, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Ammar Awad)

TEL AVIV: Israeli officials are expected to question the co - pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a co mmercial passenger flight from Dubai bound for Tel Aviv, ac co rding to a source briefed on the investigation. Disaster was averted on flydubai flight FZ1073 on Wednesday (Sep 30) after passengers and crew subdued the co - pilot , who had stabbed the captain in what Israeli officials have said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying over 170 passengers and crew. A reserve flydubai pilot crew travelling on the flight landed the plane at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co - pilot was detained by Saudi Arabian authorities. The co - pilot was transferred on Thursday to the UAE, where the source said Israeli officials were expected to question him.

The source declined to say which Israeli agency or authority would take part in the question ing. Asked whether Israeli officials would question the co - pilot , an Israeli government official told Reuters that Israeli investigators would take part in the UAE-led investigation alongside Emirati authorities, seeking to determine what happened and examine the suspect's motives and background. The UAE foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for co mment on whether Israeli officials would question the co - pilot .

Related:

Trump vows to hit Iran 'very hard' if linked to flydubai attack

In his first public co mments on the incident, flydubai Chief Executive Ghaith Al Ghaith said on Friday that authorities were co nducting an official investigation, supported by the airline, after what he described as a "safety incident" in the co ckpit. "It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts," he said in a written statement, acknowledging that there were "many question s" about what happened on flight FZ1073. The UAE state news agency reported on Thursday that Emirati authorities had opened an investigation seeking to establish the circumstances and motives and determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction".

MOTIVE NOT YET ESTABLISHED Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that Israel was looking into whether the co - pilot had acted under anyone's direction, warning in a video statement released by his office that whoever was involved would pay a "heavy price". Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals. Netanyahu on Thursday said that the co - pilot , whom he has identified as an Omani national, had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination" and was clearly suicidal, but that so far a motive for his actions had not been established. Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has said pilot s from such co untries were not permitted to operate flight s to Israel. It was not clear how the co - pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv. The aircraft plunged some 16,625 feet in just over 30 se co nds as it flew over Saudi Arabia on the journey from the United Arab Emirates to Israel, ac co rding to data from flight tracker Flight radar24. The route is popular among Israeli s.

CAPTAIN HAILED AS HERO The co - pilot 's identity has not been publicly disclosed beyond his nationality. The captain who was stabbed has been identified as Indian national Smit Machchhar, who has been hailed as a hero by Netanyahu and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi . Omani authorities have not co mmented on the incident. The incident heightened security fears in Israel weeks before Israeli s vote on Oct 27, in the first general election since the Hamas-led attacks on Oct 7, 2023, with Israel's security featuring prominently in the campaigning. The US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February, in a war that quickly spread to the Gulf and Lebanon, where Israel has been fighting Iran-backed militant group Hezbollah. Since co ming under attack by Iran this year, the UAE has strengthened its relationships with Israel, with which it opened ties as a result of the 2020 Abraham Ac co rds.

Related:

'I could not let all those people die': Wounded flydubai pilot describes moment he realised plane was going down

item.title: Euroleague to debate NBA tie-up as Europe basketball future hangs in balance
item.description: The clock is ticking for the NBA and Euroleague to find common ground in time for a joint launch next year, as the North American titan eyes an expansion across the Atlantic that could alter the ecosystem of European basketball.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow, Amy Tennery, Frank Pingue
item.content:encoded: The clock is ticking for the NBA and Euroleague to find common ground in time for a joint launch next year, as the North American titan eyes an expansion across the Atlantic that could alter the ecosystem of European basketball. Euroleague shareholders are due to meet on Monday in Italy to discuss a proposal that would see it join forces with the National Basketball Association, rather than compete against one another. The upcoming discussions at Lake Como represent a fork in the road for the future of European basketball: Should a merger be agreed, it would represent a significant shift in governance, structure and the financing of Europe’s continental competition. If no agreement is found, NBA Europe and the Euroleague are set to enter into a rivalry, with the latter intending to alter the existing format, expanding the competition in the process. "This is a unique opportunity historically to bring all sides together - including FIBA - and reshape the European basketball ecosystem," Lega Basket Serie A President Maurizio Gherardini told Reuters. Euroleague is crafting its own expansion project while the NBA is barrelling forward with an expected 16-team league that would include 10-12 permanent franchises and four to six spots available through qualification. The NBA has made clear it intends to launch in 2027 whether or not an agreement is reached, leaving Euroleague clubs to decide whether they are better served joining forces with the new competition or trying to withstand it. A Euroleague spokesperson said conversations with the NBA were focused on a path forward that would see the two work together. NBA READY TO MOVE FORWARD A picture of what an NBA Europe would look like is beginning to emerge. Teams would come from three pathways, including existing clubs, franchises launched by outside investors and clubs founded by existing European soccer teams. "QSI has been approached … maybe two years ago," Paris St Germain owner Qatar Sports Investments told Reuters. "We’ve been actively involved in discussions for at least a year." Real Madrid, AC Milan and Barcelona, which have also been named. as potential affiliate clubs for NBA Europe teams, did not respond to a request for comment. The NBA's managing director for Europe and the Middle East, George Aivazoglou, is due to provide a public update on talks at a summit in London on Thursday. "All bidders, including football clubs, are not rushing into it since the Euroleague’s position is not yet clear," a source familiar with the discussions told Reuters. 'INJECTION OF MONEY' The NBA previously [USN:L1N3QQ016 TEXT:"told Reuters"] it believes the sport is lagging behind its potential across the continent. NBA Europe would also align domestic league and national team schedules, allowing players to represent club and country year-round and resolve scheduling conflicts that exist. Euroleague enjoys robust attendance and fanbases but lacks permanent teams in some major markets, with criticism over stadium infrastructure a longstanding sticking point. "They're gonna bring an injection of money, of professionalism in the way they treat their players," player-turned-agent Pete Mickeal told Reuters. Mickeal played several years in the EuroLeague and won the championship in 2010. "Every single player that ever played in Europe has had a money issue. These are the things that I think, when the NBA comes in, that's gonna change." Mickeal also pointed to the multi-billion-dollar league's superior marketing and resources to bring teams to major-market cities. "They have everything at their fingertips," said Mickeal, who heads his Mickeal Sports Group agency. "Everything is right there for them to go get it." NBA Europe has identified potential locations for 12 anchor teams, targeting London, Paris, Rome, Milan, Berlin, Munich, Istanbul, Madrid, Athens, Barcelona, Manchester, and Lyon, The Athletic said. Were the Euroleague to execute their expansion plan, it would see the current 20-team competition gain four teams next season. A maximum of eight 'long-term' franchises would join the existing 13, the rest filled out by temporary members. The Euroleague told Reuters that 14 bids had been received for those eight spots amounting to more than €800 million ($901.36 million) in franchise fees. Under the NBA Europe proposal, not all of the 13 permanent Euroleague teams would be guaranteed a spot. The NBA says it will award franchises and set entry fees on a case-by-case basis, but media reports said they had received several bids in the $500 million to $1 billion range. ($1 = 0.8875 euros)

item.title: ＥＣＢ副総裁、銀行規制の簡素化提案 資本要件緩和には否定的
item.description: [フランクフルト ２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[フランクフルト　２日　ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のブイチッチ副総裁は２日、欧州の銀行業界から見直しを求める声が出ている銀行規制について「堅固さを確保するために必ずしも複雑なルールが必要だとは思わない」と述べ、簡素化する構えを示した。一方、「現在の資本要件の水準は、欧州の銀行にとって競争上不利に働いていない」とし、要件緩和には否定的な見解を示した。

簡素化の具体策として、資本算定に関する「キャピタル・スタック（資本積み上げ）」と呼ばれるさまざまな要件を「解除可能なバッファー」と「解除不可能なバッファー」の２つに整理する考えを示した。中小銀行についてはコスト負担を軽減するため、より簡素な規制の枠組みを設けるべきだと主張した。

欧州の銀行の経営状況については、健全性を保っており、欧州にとっての強みになっていると述べ、「堅固な金融システムこそが、持続可能な経済成長のための前提条件となる」との見解を示した。

このほか、銀行の破綻処理の枠組みを簡素化することも提案した。

item.title: Judge warns AI could stunt lawyers' training and harm their clients
item.description: A federal judge has warned that law firms' increasing use of artificial intelligence could create risks for clients and hinder the training of junior lawyers, even as he declined to sanction attorneys over AI-generated errors in a court filing.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A federal judge has warned that law firms' increasing use of artificial intelligence could create risks for clients and hinder the training of junior lawyers, even as he declined to sanction attorneys over AI-generated errors in a court filing. Manhattan-based US District Judge Arun Subramanian said in an order this week that the episode should serve as a "wakeup call" for lawyers, cautioning that AI-generated legal work must be carefully checked for accuracy. "While clients may demand the use of AI to save money, there is a risk of adverse consequences when things go wrong," Subramanian wrote. "For this reason, it might make sense to clients to think hard before requiring counsel to use AI for tasks such as the drafting of briefs." The judge did not say the client in this case had requested its lawyers use AI. State and federal judges [USN:L6N42308A TEXT:"increasingly are weighing"] whether and how to sanction lawyers over their misuse of AI as the technology becomes more widespread. In the New York case, Subramanian in an order last month questioned whether "unchecked" use of AI led to citation errors in a copyright infringement case he was overseeing. The judge this week declined to impose sanctions on the lawyers after Cynthia Arato, an attorney for defendant Foundation Media, apologized and said the errors stemmed from another lawyer at her firm who was responsible for preparing the initial draft and finalizing it before it was filed. Arato said in a declaration this week that the lawyer, who was not named in Arato's declaration, acted "contrary to the firm's policies and training" and that the failure to check AI-generated citations was "an isolated error and not any bad faith or intent to mislead or deceive the court." Foundation Media declined to comment. There was no indication in court filings that the company had directed its outside lawyers to use AI. Arato said her firm, Shapiro Arato Bach, was implementing further safeguards against AI misuse. In a filing submitted on Thursday, Arato disclosed that the firm had used AI tools created by technology company Harvey to help prepare the improperly vetted filing. Harvey declined to comment. Subramanian said in his order that the legal profession should "think about ways to ensure that junior lawyers are getting the training they need, even as reliance on these technological tools increases." He suggested that firms could require initial drafts of briefs to be prepared without AI assistance. "The use of AI may be unavoidable, but mentoring young lawyers is a joint responsibility that we all share," Subramanian wrote. item.title: Legal sector outpaced US jobs growth in September
item.description: The US legal sector reached another record employment high in September, even as job growth across the broader economy slowed more than expected last month, according to new figures released Friday by the US Department of Labor.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: The US legal sector reached another record employment high in September, even as job growth across the broader economy [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"slowed more than expected"] last month, according to new figures released Friday by the US Department of Labor. Here are the details: The Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 1,249,000 legal sector jobs in September, including lawyers, paralegals, judges and legal assistants, up 2,000 jobs from August and 7.6% higher than five years earlier US employers overall added just 29,000 jobs last month, the Labor Department reported Friday, fewer than the 90,000 that economists had expected The US finance sector, which is larger and an important source of income for law firms, lost 7,000 jobs last month. That sector has shrunk by 129,000 jobs since peaking in May 2025

item.title: 世界食料価格、9月は約4年ぶり高水準 物流混乱や悪天候響く＝ＦＡＯ
item.description:
Gus Trompiz
［パリ ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Gus Trompiz

［パリ　２日　ロイター］ - 国連食糧農業機関（ＦＡＯ）が２日発表した９月の世界食料価格指数は１３６．０ポイントと、２０２２年１１月以来、３年１０カ月ぶりの高水準となった。物流の混乱や悪天候が影響し、８月改定値の１３４．０ポイントから上昇した。

エルニーニョ現象が収穫量に影響するとの懸念から、国際的に取引される砂糖の価格は１年半ぶりの高値を付けているほか、ロシアとウクライナの戦闘激化に伴う黒海からの輸出停滞が響き、９月初めには小麦先物価格が約３年ぶりの高値を記録している。

ＦＡＯのチーフエコノミスト、マキシモ・トレロ氏は声明で「ホルムズ海峡や黒海での混乱が気候関連の要因と重なり、エネルギーや輸送、主要食品の価格に上昇圧力がかかっている。広範囲で根強い上昇傾向が見られる」と指摘。「特に輸入国では消費者への食品価格の転嫁が見られるだろう」と警告した。

砂糖価格指数は前月から６．１％、穀物価格は５．１％それぞれ上昇した。黒海で続く輸送の混乱に加え、米産トウモロコシの収穫見通しの引き下げが要因。植物油価格は０．９％上昇。一方、肉類価格は１．１％低下した。

ＦＡＯは別の報告書で、２６年の世界穀物生産量を２９億７９００万トンと予測。過去最高だった２５年に次ぐ水準となる見通しだ。

item.title: NY governor attacks law enforcement's handling of 2024 Cornell rape investigation
item.description: Kathy Hochul faulted police and prosecutors for failing to fully investigate an alleged gang rape in 2024 at Cornell University, saying she was "deeply disturbed" by how the incident was handled.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: New York Governor Kathy Hochul on Friday faulted police and prosecutors for failing to fully investigate an [USN:L1N45N0UA TEXT:"alleged gang rape"] in 2024 at Cornell University, saying she was "deeply disturbed" by how the incident was handled. Hochul was speaking at a press conference alongside state Attorney General Letitia James, whom she appointed on Thursday night as a [USN:L1N45O00M TEXT:"special prosecutor"] to investigate the allegations. The case has drawn fresh scrutiny after the alleged victim filed a lawsuit accusing fraternity members of raping her while she was intoxicated, prompting widespread outrage over how the matter was handled in 2024. On Monday, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he was [USN:L1N45K0ML TEXT:"reopening"] an investigation, which will now be overseen by James' office. Van Houten has defended his office's decision in 2024 not to pursue charges, saying that the woman's sworn statement to police did not contain allegations that rose to the level of a crime under state law. New York law makes it more difficult to prosecute sexual assault cases in which the victim voluntarily became intoxicated, according to experts and advocates. Some news outlets have reported in recent days that the woman told police unequivocally that she was raped, but that investigators did not include that claim in the sworn statement that was provided to prosecutors. Hochul criticized Cornell police for that omission, while also questioning why Van Houten's office did not interview the woman directly or review the full transcript of her police interview. "This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her," Hochul said. In a statement after the press conference, Van Houten said he supported James' appointment and would cooperate with her investigation. "It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the University," he added. "The focus has been and should continue to be on the victims." A Cornell spokesperson said the school supports James' appointment and is "committed to an independent external review of all aspects of how Cornell has handled this case" but did not address Hochul's specific criticisms. In an interview with CNN, the woman's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, endorsed Hochul's decision to appoint James, saying he had little faith in local prosecutors' handling of the case. Hochul also said she would work with the state legislature to update the state's sexual assault laws and eliminate the [USN:L1N45M14T TEXT:"current distinction"] between victims who voluntarily consumed intoxicants and those given substances without their consent. Several lawmakers have already renewed calls to pass legislation addressing what they described as a loophole in the law. "If someone is too intoxicated to consent, it should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol," Hochul said.

The greenback trimmed some

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 2 : The dollar was on track for a fourth straight weekly gain against the euro on Friday, supported by elevated US Treasury yields amid a selloff in European government bond markets and expectations the Federal Reserve will maintain its hawkish interest rate stance.  The greenback trimmed some of its recent gains after data showed US job growth in September fell short of economists' expectations and the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2 per cent. Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields also slipped after the report before rising 5.14 basis points to 5.285 per cent. Still, the dollar remained underpinned by US yields that are hovering near multi-decade highs, rising concerns over the fiscal outlook in parts of Europe, and higher oil prices. The increase in crude prices has prompted some investors to reduce exposure to currencies of major energy importers, including the euro and the yen. The euro is on track for its fourth straight week of losses against the dollar, the longest such stretch since mid-May 2025. It was last up 0.13 per cent at $1.12580.

"When I look at the (jobs) data in aggregate, I think about it as actually a Goldilocks set of numbers: so activity is still pretty resilient but it's not generating significant inflationary pressure," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura. "That's a good backdrop from a broad economic perspective. It should be a relatively good number for risk assets in general and for high beta currencies. It also probably at the margin doesn't have a huge impact on Fed pricing, but it removes a little bit of tail risk as to whether they would hike again in October." The US central bank raised rates and signaled more hikes after the end of its policy meeting last month, with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reaffirming monetary policy independence despite repeated calls from US President Donald Trump for lower borrowing costs. Markets responded by raising their bets on further tightening. Traders are pricing in an 86 per cent chance that the Fed will hold rates steady later this month, compared with 36 per cent a week earlier, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The dollar weakened 0.30 per cent to 0.8285 against the Swiss franc. It was also down 0.15 per cent to 157.81 against the Japanese yen, but on track for its third straight weekly increase.  The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was down 0.1 per cent to 101.88. It is set for its third straight weekly gain. EUROPEAN WORRIES European countries on Friday agreed to release diesel stocks.  US President Donald Trump had pressured governments to do so, in a bid to cool surging fuel prices linked to the Iran war. Euro zone inflation is likely to increase in the coming months, keeping pressure on the European Central Bank to raise rates. French and Italian government bonds have come under selling pressure in recent weeks amid expectations of rising policy rates and growing political risk as 2027 elections loom, with French 10-year yields jumping on Thursday to their highest level since 2002. The premium of French 10-year government bond yields over safe-haven German ones rose to above 150 basis points on Friday, its highest since late 2011, as worries about France's finances and political turmoil grew. The euro was down 0.15 per cent against the Swiss franc to 0.9327 but was flat at 177.67 against the Japanese yen. The single currency is headed for weekly losses against both the Swiss franc and the yen. "For all the hand wringing on France risks, EUR/CHF resilience stood out until this week's sharp selloff. Skew premium in risk reversals has similarly widened out to historical extremes," said Bank of America analysts in an investor note.

item.title: 米沿岸警備隊、キューバへ向かう燃料輸送船を拿捕 石油禁輸措置続く中
item.description:
Katharine Jackson
[ワシントン ２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Katharine Jackson

[ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - 米沿岸警備隊は２日、燃料を積んでキューバに向かっていた大型貨物船を拿捕（だほ）したと発表した。トランプ米政権によるキューバへの厳しい石油禁輸措置が続く中での動きとなる。

沿岸警備隊によると、同船は９月５日、キューバとメキシコの間のカリブ海で、当局の追跡を逃れようと航行していたところを拿捕された。ニューヨーク・タイムズ紙は、同船の全長が約９１メートルであると報じた。

沿岸警備隊は声明で「同船は燃料を積載してキューバへ向かっていた。ダークフリート（闇の船団）の間で一般的な手口を用いていたとみられる」と説明した。

声明によると、沿岸警備隊の部隊が同船に乗り込み、メキシコへ護送した。メキシコ海軍の検査チームは「同船のバラストタンク内に大量の燃料があることを確認した。また、違法な燃料が入っているとみられる複数のコンテナも積載していた」としている。

ただ、当局がどのように燃料がキューバ向けだと把握したか、また同船がどれだけの燃料を積載していたかには言及していない。

トランプ政権はキューバの体制転換を目標としていると公言している。今年に入って発動された米国による石油封鎖を受け、同国は燃料不足や停電など深刻な打撃を受けている。

Dutch eyewear chain Hans Anders halts sale of Meta glasses, citing privacy concerns

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wears the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, as he delivers a speech presenting the new line of smart glasses, during the Meta Connect event at the company's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, on Sep 17, 2025. (File photo: Reuters/Carlos Barria)

FAST

AMSTERDAM: One of the largest Dutch eyewear retail chains said on Friday (Oct 2) it had suspended sales of Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium amid growing privacy concerns, in one of the first such moves by a retailer. "This decision follows the ongoing public and political debate surrounding smart glasses and the questions being raised about the conditions under which this technology can be used," a spokesperson for the Hans Anders chain said. A growing Dutch outcry over the glasses mirrors a broader backlash against smart glasses equipped with cameras. In Britain, pub chain Wetherspoon has restricted use of Meta's glasses over concerns about covert recording, while Meta and Luxottica face a US suit alleging videos captured by the glasses were viewed by human annotators without the knowledge of people filmed.

A Meta spokesperson said the company is continuing to develop the popular glasses. "Every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that blinks when you take a photo or video — it can't be turned off, and the camera is disabled if someone covers or tampers with it," they said.   In the Netherlands, privacy regulator AP last month warned that videos made with smart glasses showing identifiable people cannot generally be shared or published without their permission, which would be difficult to obtain in a public place.  Consumer rights group Consumentenbond this week said it would take Meta to court unless the company changes the glasses to comply with privacy law. Offlimits, a group that combats online abuse, on Friday also urged Meta and Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica to voluntarily remove the glasses from sale until a way can be found to make surreptitious recordings impossible. EssilorLuxottica could not immediately be reached for comment. Hans Anders is a subsidiary of Nexeye, which is owned by private equity firm KKR. Nexeye operates 776 stores across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Sweden. It does not sell the glasses in the latter three countries.

FAST

GENEVA: Three-in-four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the "absolutely devastating" impact of a surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said on Friday (Oct 2). Yemen is experiencing the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthi group since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. The renewed conflict could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes. Within just a few weeks, the fighting has driven the share of households without sufficient food to 74% in government-controlled areas accessible to WFP, the UN hunger body's Assistant Executive Director for Programme Operations told reporters in Geneva. The total population of government-held areas is estimated at around 10 million people. “The effect of this latest flare-up of insecurity on the food security situation threatens to be absolutely devastating,” Hollingworth told reporters in Geneva via video link from Rome.

The Houthis, who already control most of northern Yemen including the capital Sanaa, seized the country's entire Red Sea coast last month from Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government, based in the southern port of Aden. Displaced families are arriving outside Aden and around the mountain city of Taiz without any water or food, as many had to leave everything behind, WFP said.

Related:

Houthis say Saudi strikes on Yemen's Taiz leave dozens of casualties

Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone attack on Madinah

Prices of basic food staples such as wheat flour and vegetable oil are rising in a country that imports around 90 per cent of its food. “We are looking at a hunger crisis that is going to grow as it persists,” Hollingworth said, adding that frontline areas like Taiz were increasingly hard to access due to the fighting. WFP said it was scaling up its response but unless it gets around US$109 million in funding within a few weeks it will run out of food stocks and money to help the 152,000 newly displaced persons inside the country, as well as the 1.4 million people it is already supporting. Hollingworth also pointed to the potential ripple effects of disruption to two major chokepoints in the Middle East: the Bab el-Mandeb Strait near Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula. That, as well as disruption in the Black Sea due to the Ukraine-Russia conflict, risk driving up food and fuel prices and deepening food insecurity globally. A new analysis published by UN Women on Friday said an additional 11.7 million women and girls across 28 countries including Yemen, Sudan and Lebanon could face food insecurity by the end of the year, due to escalation in the Middle East and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: Ｇ７、石油備蓄1億バレル協調放出へ 当初は軽油重点で市場安定化狙う
item.description: [パリ ２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[パリ ２日 ロイター] - 主要７カ国（Ｇ７）は２日の首脳共同声明で、世界のエネルギー市場の安定化に向け、国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）を通じてディーゼル燃料（軽油）などの石油備蓄１億バレルを協調放出すると発表した。直ちに開始し、４カ月間にわたって実施する。

Ｇ７議長国のフランス大統領府が公表した声明によると、Ｇ７加盟国とパートナー国は最初の２０日間に大量の軽油を重点的に放出する。マクロン仏大統領は、放出対象は軽油と原油で、規模は最大１億バレルになると説明した。

放出する原油、軽油、その他の製品の内訳は示されていないほか、どの国が参加するのか明記されていない。声明は「今後数日中にＩＥＡの枠組みにおいて会合を開き、必要に応じて軽油の追加放出の可能性について協議する」とした。

Ｇ７の発表に先立ち、トランプ米大統領は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で「欧州は大量に備蓄しているディーゼルを大規模に放出することに合意した。手続きは直ちに開始される」と表明していた。

Ｇ７はまた、加盟各国の製油所の保守点検日程を調整する方針を表明。ＩＥＡに対し、２０２６年３月のコミットメントが直ちにかつ完全に履行されるよう監視することを要請した。

エネルギーおよびエネルギー製品について、Ｇ７諸国間で輸出制限を控えるとの約束を再確認。全ての生産国に対し、市場の緊張を悪化させかねない禁止措置を導入しないよう求めた。

マクロン氏は、ホルムズ海峡を通じたエネルギー供給の確保に向け、引き続き行動を調整することで合意したと述べた。

声明はイランによる近隣諸国への攻撃を改めて非難し、ロシアに対する制裁を維持する方針も示した。

トランプ氏はアラバマ州に向け出発する前にホワイトハウスで記者団に対し、米国はディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止措置を導入しないと表明。そうした計画は一度も検討されたことがないとした上で、「欧州にはディーゼル燃料が大量にあり、世界に大きく貢献するだろう。米国も同様だ。われわれは輸出禁止措置は講じない。やるべきことをやるだけだ」と述べた。トランプ氏は過去２週間に輸出禁止を検討していると複数回発言しており、支持する考えも示していた。

item.title: Chinese auto show debuts in Argentina as sales surge
item.description: Buenos Aires is hosting its first Chinese auto show on Friday as Argentina’s car market under President Javier Milei has shifted from heavy protectionism to a more open and competitive environment.
item.dc:creator: Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: Buenos Aires is hosting its first Chinese auto show on Friday as Argentina’s car market under President Javier Milei has shifted from heavy protectionism to a more open and competitive environment. Chinese brands are flooding the market, benefiting from a measure that allows in up to 50,000 electric and hybrid vehicles without tariffs in 2026. Chinese brands accounted for 10% of car and light commercial vehicle sales in Argentina in August, up from about 2% late last year. Since launching in Argentina [USN:L6N3VO0YF TEXT:"in late 2025"], China's electric vehicle maker BYD (002594.SZ) has become the ninth best-selling car brand. The company leads electric car sales in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay. At the auto show, more than 20 Chinese brands, including [USN:L4N45E0BT TEXT:"Geely"] (0175.HK) , Chery (9973.HK) , GWM (601633.SS) and [USN:L1N45K00B TEXT:"Dongfeng"], were on display. German Molina, a 3D designer who already owns a Chinese car and wants to buy another, looked around with his wife and son. "If you go out onto the main avenues or neighborhoods, you see a large number of Chinese cars, and it’s not just one brand, but many different ones," said Molina. "I believe it’s only a matter of time before people start embracing them a bit more." Sebastian Beato, president of Argentina’s auto dealers’ association ACARA, said the "impressive" growth among Chinese brands had pushed the national industry to produce new models, such as the [USN:L8N4500PL TEXT:"Renault Niagara"] pick-up truck unveiled in September. Earlier this week the Argentine government said Japanese automaker Toyota Motor (7203.T) would [USN:L6N45M1A7 TEXT:"invest"] $1.34 billion to develop an EV plant in Argentina. If Argentina's auto industry doesn’t transform, "it’s going to have obsolete cars," Beato said. MILEI UNCONCERNED Chinese automakers are steadily expanding across Latin America, selling both traditional vehicles and EVs at a pace that has alarmed some local markets. Brazil and Mexico have introduced tariffs aimed at slowing the influx and protecting domestic manufacturing jobs. But Milei, a libertarian, has said he is unconcerned by the rapid growth of BYD and dismissed suggestions that it could complicate his close relationship with the US during an interview last month. "What Argentines buy is the problem of Argentines," Milei told Bloomberg at the Economic Club of New York. Tesla in July launched operations in Uruguay, and there are signs the US automaker could soon enter Argentina. The registration of Tesla Argentina appeared in the country's official gazette in April, and state energy company YPF said in June it had signed a letter of intent with Tesla to explore [USN:S0N41Q00Y TEXT:"energy storage"] opportunities. Tesla did not respond to a request for comment. 'POSSIBILITY TO COMPETE' Car sales in Argentina have fallen 13% so far this year from the same period in 2025, a decline that industry analysts attribute to a market adjustment after last year's strong growth was fueled by lower trade barriers. High interest rates have also dissuaded consumers from taking out car loans. Andres Civetta, an economist at consultancy Abeceb, said Argentina's auto industry should focus on pick-up trucks, where the country has established a strong export position and doesn't yet face competition from Chinese brands. Fernando Rodriguez Canedo, executive director of Argentina's association of car factories, welcomed Milei's gradual rollback of national export duties and said the industry was also pressing provincial governments to reduce local taxes. "That would give us the possibility to compete," Canedo said.

item.title: 米韓、エネ事業巡り食い違い トランプ氏「勇み足でない」
item.description: [ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２日、韓国との通商合意に８４億ドル規模の石油増進回収（ＥＯＲ）プロジェクトが含まれると明らかにした。ただ、
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２日、韓国との通商合意に８４億ドル規模の石油増進回収（ＥＯＲ）プロジェクトが含まれると明らかにした。ただ、 韓国の聨合ニュースは産業通商資源省高官の話として、同プロジェクトは両国間の戦略的投資協定の一環ではないと報じた。

トランプ大統領は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」に「韓国との合意は一段と改善している！石油増進回収プロジェクトに８４億ドルが投じられる。石油・ガスの増産は、米国のエネルギー覇権と将来に向けた世界のエネルギー安全保障につながる！」と投稿した。

聨合ニュースによると、韓国産業通商省の当局者は、合意の範囲は両国政府が２０２５年１１月に発表した共同ファクトシートの内容に限られ、石油増進回収事業は含まれていないと述べた。

トランプ氏は１１月の中間選挙を前に経済・投資案件を経済面の実績としてアピールしている。

９月３０日には、韓国が米国内の事業に約２０００億ドルを投資すると発表した。ただ、投資計画の柱の一つとされたアラスカ州の液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）事業向けの５４０億ドル規模のパイプライン建設について、韓国政府は、現時点で確定したものではないと説明した。ＬＮＧ事業計画は採算性と法的手続きの順守を評価する審査を受ける予定で、一定の商業的・法的条件が満たされた場合に限って進めるとしている。

アラスカのＬＮＧ事業は数十年前から計画されているが、いまだに投資の確約を得られていない。

トランプ氏は２日、韓国による投資を発表したことについて「勇み足ではない」とホワイトハウスで記者団に述べた。「韓国側はその場にいて、代表者もいた」とし、韓国が投資を見送れば、追加関税を課すことになると警告した。

item.title: 米製造業新規受注、8月は0.1％の小幅増 民間航空機が重し
item.description: [ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - 米商務省が２日発表した８月の製造業新規受注は前月比０．１％増の小幅な伸びにとどまっ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米製造業新規受注、8月は0.1％の小幅増　民間航空機が重し 10/2 23:45 配信

米ワシントン州エベレットにある航空機大手ボーイングの工場。７月撮影。Jennifer Buchanan/Seattle Times

[ワシントン　２日　ロイター] - 米商務省が２日発表した８月の製造業新規受注は前月比０．１％増の小幅な伸びにとどまった。電気機器・家電製品・同部品への強い需要があったものの、低調な民間航空機の受注に相殺された。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は０．１％増だった。

７月は０．９％増から０．８％増に下方改定された。

８月は前年同月比では６．８％増加した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）インフラの拡充に加え、堅調な国内需要に対応するため企業が在庫を再構築していることが製造業の下支えとなっている。ただ、米国とイスラエルによるイランとの戦争がサプライチェーン（供給網）を混乱させ、エネルギー価格を押し上げている中で、ＡＩ投資ブームと関連性の薄い分野は今後数カ月間、苦戦を強いられる可能性があるとの懸念もある。

８月は、民間航空機・同部品の受注が４．３％減少したことが重しとなった。自動車車体・同部品・トレーラーの受注は０．８％増。機械受注は１．１％増加した。コンピューター・電子製品の受注は横ばいだった一方、前年同月比では１４．７％増加した。電気機器・家電製品・同部品の受注は１．１％急増した。

企業の設備投資計画の指標とされる航空機を除く非国防資本財（コア資本財）の受注は１．６％増と、先月発表の速報値から変わらずだった。コア資本財の出荷は０．５％増と、当初発表の０．６％増から下方改定された。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米株高支える高い増益、投資家は持続可能性に不安も 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：出遅れ気味の米不動産株、持ち直し期待高まる 焦点：後退する米企業役員の多様性、トランプ米大統領の政策反映 コラム：「米国例外主義」なお健在、外国投資家のテック株流入持続が示唆 最終更新: 10/2(金) 23:45 ロイター

item.title: 新会社名は「スカイダンス」、パラマウントのＷＢＤ買収完了後＝ＣＥＯ
item.description: [２日 ロイター] - 米メディア大手パラマウント・スカイダンスのデービッド・エリソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２日...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
新会社名は「スカイダンス」、パラマウントのＷＢＤ買収完了後＝ＣＥＯ 10/2 23:40 配信

2025年12月8日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

[２日 ロイター] - 米メディア大手パラマウント・スカイダンスのデービッド・エリソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２日、ワーナー・ブラザース・ディスカバリー（ＷＢＤ）買収が来週にも完了次第、統合後の新会社名を「スカイダンス」とすると明らかにした。

エリソン氏はソーシャルメディアへの投稿で、パラマウントとワーナー・ブラザースの両映画スタジオの個別のアイデンティティーが失われないようにすることが目的で、新たな企業ブランドの下に統合するものではないと説明した。

その上で、「統合後の会社に独自のアイデンティティーを与えつつ、パラマウントとワーナー・ブラザースをはじめとする優れたブランドが引き続きスポットライトを浴び続けられる名称を望んでいた」と述べた。

item.title: 欧州がディーゼル備蓄放出で合意、トランプ氏 価格抑制へ米が圧力
item.description: [ワシントン ２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２日、イラン戦争を背景とした燃料価格の高騰を抑制するよう求める米国の圧力を受け、欧州がディーゼル（軽油）燃料の備蓄を放出することで合意したと明らかにした。

トランプ大統領は「欧州は大量に備蓄しているディーゼルを大規模に放出することに合意した。手続きは直ちに開始される」と自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」に投稿した。

関係筋の１人がロイターに語ったところによると、米国はフランスやドイツを含む欧州の主要国に対し、２０日以内に１億バレルのディーゼルを放出するよう要求した。

フランスのエリゼ宮（大統領府）によると、マクロン仏大統領は１日夜、トランプ大統領と電話会談を行い、燃料価格の高騰に対処し、精製石油製品の世界的な供給を確保するために協力する必要性を強調した。こうした中、ＥＵ加盟国は２日、欧州諸国が５０００万バレルのディーゼルを、国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）加盟国が５０００万バレルの原油を放出するという仏の提案について協議したと関係筋は話している。

マクロン仏大統領はその後、主要７カ国（Ｇ７）首脳とのビデオ会議を開催し、エネルギー情勢について協議した。

item.title: トランプ氏、ＡＩ責任者にクレイトン国家情報長官起用か＝報道
item.description: [ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が、クレイトン国家情報長官を人工知能（ＡＩ）担当責任者「ＡＩツ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トランプ氏、ＡＩ責任者にクレイトン国家情報長官起用か＝報道 10/2 23:19 配信

クレイトン米国家情報長官。7月15日、ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Nathan Howard

[ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が、クレイトン国家情報長官を人工知能（ＡＩ）担当責任者「ＡＩツァー（czar）」に指名する見通しであることが分かった。ＣＮＮが２日、関係筋の話として報じた。

トランプ大統領は９月、新たなＡＩ担当責任者を任命し、「ＡＩフォース（force）」を創設する計画を明らかにしていた。

トランプ政権２期目の発足当初は、ベンチャーキャピタリストのデービッド・サックス氏がＡＩツァーを務めていたが、その後辞任し、現在は外部顧問を務めている。

item.title: US job growth slows sharply in September; unemployment rate rises to 4.2%
item.description: WASHINGTON: US job growth slowed more than expected in September and the nonfarm payrolls count for the prior two months was revised sharply lower, almost taking another interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this month off the table.The Labor Department's closely watched employment report on Friday (Oct
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

US job growth slows sharply in September; unemployment rate rises to 4.2%

A job seeker waits to talk to a recruiter at a job fair on Aug 28, 2025, in Sunrise, Florida. (Photo: AP/Marta Lavandier)

FAST

WASHINGTON: US job growth slowed more than expected in September and the nonfarm payrolls count for the prior two months was revised sharply lower, almost taking another interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this month off the table. The Labor Department's closely watched employment report on Friday (Oct 2) also showed the unemployment rate increased to 4.2 per cent last month from 4.1 per cent in August as more people entered the workforce. The sharp moderation in job growth likely does not mark a sudden deterioration in labour market conditions. Economists noted that payrolls have a tendency to underperform when the Labor Day holiday falls relatively late in September, as was the case this year. There have been no signs of a broad increase in layoffs. First-time applications for unemployment benefits have been hovering at 57-year lows amid robust corporate profit growth and resilient domestic demand. Economists said the report reaffirmed the labour market's "low-hire, low-fire" state and likely had no impact on near-term monetary policy, with inflation remaining the key focus.

"This is a disappointing jobs report and a reminder that the low-hire, low-fire labour market never went away," said Olu Sonola, head of US economics at Fitch Ratings. "Weak job growth, a slightly higher unemployment rate, contained wage gains and downward revisions to earlier payroll estimates give the Fed little reason to keep an October rate hike on the table. But CPI remains the report that matters most." Nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised rise of 133,000 in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls would advance by 90,000 after a previously reported surge of 162,000 in August. Estimates ranged from as low as 35,000 to as high as 180,000. The data for July was revised to show the economy shed 10,000 jobs, the second time this year that payrolls turned negative. All told, the economy added 60,000 fewer jobs in July and August than previously estimated. Volatility linked to the model the government uses to strip out seasonal fluctuations from the data likely accounted for both the meagre payroll gains last month and the downward revision to the count for August. Economists, however, said they expected growing headwinds from the US-Israel war with Iran, including high energy prices and strained supply chains, would start disrupting the labour market by the end of this year and into 2027. Diesel prices are at record highs and could start to exert pressure beyond the transportation and agricultural sectors. Ongoing tariffs also are a source of concern, with an Institute for Supply Management survey on Thursday showing rising anxiety among manufacturers over the trade war with Canada. HEALTHCARE PAYROLLS RISE MARGINALLY Healthcare continued to account for the bulk of the job growth, adding 17,000 positions, a figure that was well below the average monthly gain of 33,000 in the past 12 months. Those job gains occurred in ambulatory healthcare services and at hospitals. Employment in nursing and residential care facilities dropped by 9,000 positions, which could be related to the termination of Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of thousands of Haitian immigrants. Construction payrolls increased by 11,000, while manufacturers added 9,000. Financial activities employment dropped by 7,000 positions. Despite job growth almost stalling last month, the average workweek was unchanged at 34.4 hours. Financial markets further reduced bets on a rate hike at the US central bank's Oct 27-28 meeting to roughly 13 per cent, down from 22 per cent prior to the report and about 69 per cent a week ago, CME Group's FedWatch tool showed. The odds of further monetary policy tightening had already been diminished by cooler-than-expected inflation readings for August and July. The Fed last month raised its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75-4.00 per cent range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs ahead. With inflation still above the central bank's 2 per cent target, economists continued to expect a rate hike in December. US stocks opened higher. The dollar slipped against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields were mostly lower. The rise in the unemployment rate reflected a jump of 485,000 in the labour force. This lifted the labour force participation rate to 61.8 per cent last month from 61.6 per cent in August. Household employment increased by 406,000.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: テスラの世界納車、第3四半期は市場予想上回る 欧州で需要回復
item.description:
Anhata Rooprai Akash Sriram
[２日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラが２日発...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
テスラの世界納車、第3四半期は市場予想上回る　欧州で需要回復 10/2 23:16 配信

フランス・パリ近郊にあるテスラの納車センター。2025年4月撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Anhata Rooprai　Akash Sriram

[２日　ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラが２日発表した第３・四半期（７─９月期）の世界納車台数は４８万６５３２台と、市場予想を上回った。欧州での需要回復が、米国での税制優遇措置の失効や中国での競争激化による影響を相殺した。

同社の株価は午前の取引で約４％超上昇した。

ビジブル・アルファがまとめたアナリスト予想平均は４５万６８９６台だった。今年初めとは異なり、アナリストらは納車台数の通年予想を引き上げている。２０２６年の納車台数は１８２万台と、６月時点のコンセンサス予想の１６５万台から上方修正した。

ただ、納車台数が３年連続で前年比減となる事態を回避するには、同社は第４・四半期に少なくとも３１万１４４８台を納車する必要がある。

欧州では昨年、イーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の政治的言動への反発などから販売が低迷したものの、欧州連合（ＥＵ）での新車登録台数は８月までで約３分の２増加。フランスでは「モデルＹ」が全車種を通じて最も売れた車となった。

モーニングスターのアナリスト、セス・ゴールドスタイン氏は「この堅調な数字により、テスラは２年連続の減少を経て、通年の納車台数が増加に転じる軌道に乗った。ＦＳＤ（完全自動運転）が、消費者が他の自動車メーカーではなくテスラを選ぶ決め手となっている」と述べた。

テスラの第３・四半期の車両生産台数は４６万４３９１台で、予想の４８万６７６１台を下回った。

item.title: 米10月利上げ観測後退、雇用統計軟調で＝金利先物市場
item.description: [２日 ロイター] - ２日発表の米雇用統計から労働市場が予想以上に減速していることが明らかとなり、米連邦準備理事会（...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米10月利上げ観測後退、雇用統計軟調で＝金利先物市場 10/2 22:41 配信

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）ビル。2025年11月撮影。REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

[２日　ロイター] - ２日発表の米雇用統計から労働市場が予想以上に減速していることが明らかとなり、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の当局者はインフレ抑制に向けた追加利上げを先送りするさらなる理由を得る形となった。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の雇用統計によると、非農業部門雇用者数は２万９０００人増で、前月から伸びが鈍化し市場予想を下回った。失業率は４．２％で前月の４．１％から上昇した。今回の統計は、トランプ大統領率いる共和党が、連邦議会上下両院の支配権を維持できるかどうかを左右する１１月の中間選挙前の、労働市場に関する最後の広範な指標となる。

雇用統計発表後、金利先物市場が織り込む、ＦＲＢが１０月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げに踏み切る確率は６分の１未満と、これまでの４分の１超から低下した。１２月の利上げ観測も後退したものの、年内の利上げ実施は高い確率で織り込まれている。

ＦＲＢは先月開いたＦＯＭＣで、インフレ率を２％目標に戻すため３年２カ月ぶりとなる利上げを決定した。当局者らは、イラン戦争やその他のインフレ押し上げ要因となるショックが続く場合、労働市場が安定を保つ限り、年内に少なくともあと１回の利上げを実施する可能性が高いとの姿勢を示していた。

フィフス・サードのエコノミスト、ビル・アダムズ氏は「９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）と卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）、ガソリン価格、そして１０月の次回ＦＯＭＣまでの地政学的動向の方が、今回の雇用統計よりも次回の金利決定に大きな影響を与えるだろう」と述べた。

item.title: Fed may skip October but pull rate hike trigger in December
item.description: Federal Reserve policymakers were already leaning against delivering a second straight rate hike this month to give them time to sift through more economic data before pulling the trigger again, and a cooler than expected job market report Friday leaves that approach intact.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve policymakers were already leaning against delivering a second straight rate hike this month to give them time to sift through more economic data before pulling the trigger again, and a [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"cooler than expected job market report"] Friday leaves that approach intact. Still-to-come data, particularly the closely-watched consumer price index measure of inflation coming just before the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting, could yet shift that calculus. After increasing the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point last month to put inflation on a "timelier" path toward the Fed's 2% goal, US central bankers are now weighing the risks of moving too slowly to tamp down price pressures against potential harm to the labor market should they move too fast. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has stuck to his policy of saying nothing about where he thinks the risks lie and where rates may need to go, but his colleagues have not been so quiet . "There is plenty of room for anything to be on the table" was how Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee put it, when asked by Fox Business' Edward Lawrence if the Fed ought to raise rates or pause at their next meeting. Goolsbee said he felt latest jobs data shows the labor market is steady. "I think the inflation side of the Fed's job, that's where the problem is. We've got to keep an eye on that. We can't let that get even more out of control," Goolsbee said. US employers added just 29,000 jobs last month, the Labor Department reported Friday, less than the 90,000 economists had expected and August payroll gains were revised downward. The September unemployment rate was 4.2%, up from 4.1%. But the increase was driven by an increase in entrants to the workforce, and low unemployment insurance claims suggest there's no broad increase in layoffs. Wage growth slowed. After the Fed raised short-term borrowing costs last month, policymakers signaled they will likely deliver at least one more increase by year's end if the Iran war and other shocks that have pushed up inflation persist. Until early this week, with a peace deal elusive and trade tensions also on the front burner, expectations for a brisk series of rate hikes had been rising, along with longer-term bond yields, which hit a 24-year high on Thursday. Mortgage rates topped 7%. But speaking this week, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams said they would rather [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"see more data "]before considering further action, prompting traders to slash bets on a hike at the Fed's October meeting. Friday's report showing a deceleration in wage growth "should give comfort to Fed policymakers that the economy is not overheating in a way that calls for a hurried rate hike cycle," wrote JPMorgan chief US economist Michael Feroli. "It would now take a very strong CPI to make the October meeting live. We continue to look for another hike at the December FOMC meeting, on the assumption that the September and October price reports show still-sticky trends in core inflation." Friday's report was the last broad read of the US labor market before November elections that will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republican party keeps control of both houses of Congress. A rising cost of living amid both elevated inflation and higher borrowing costs has put voters in a sour mood about the incumbents' handling of the economy, though economic growth overall has been solid and the labor market has held in. Traders now see about a one-in-four chance of an October rate hike, and an overwhelmingly high probability of a December increase, based CME FedWatch's analysis of interest-rate futures prices. Inflation by the Fed's targeted measure was 3.4% in August, data showed this week - far above the 2% goal though not as bad as economists had projected. "The September CPI and PPI reports, prices at the pump, and geopolitical developments between now and when the Fed meets next in late October have more power to sway the next rate decision than this jobs report," wrote Fifth Third economist Bill Adams.

item.title: 米9月雇用者数2.9万人増に鈍化、失業率4.2％ 利上げ観測後退
item.description:
Lucia Mutikani
[ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が２日発表した９月の雇用統計による...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米9月雇用者数2.9万人増に鈍化、失業率4.2％　利上げ観測後退 10/2 21:58 配信

マサチューセッツ州サマービルで2022年9月撮影　REUTERS/Brian Snyder

Lucia Mutikani

[ワシントン ２日 ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が２日発表した９月の雇用統計によると、非農業部門雇用者数は２万９０００人増で、前月から伸びが鈍化し市場予想を下回った。過去２カ月分も大幅に下方改定された。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が今月の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で追加利上げに踏み切る可能性はほぼなくなったとみられる。

失業率は４．２％で、前月の４．１％から上昇した。労働市場に参入する人が増えたことが背景。ただ、非農業部門雇用者数の伸びの急減速は、労働市場の急激な悪化を示すものではないとみられる。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は９万人増、予想レンジは３万５０００─１８万人増だった。

８月の非農業部門雇用者数は１６万２０００人増から１３万３０００人増に、７月は２万１０００人増から１万人減に下方改定された。雇用者数が減少したのは２６年に入って２回目。７、８月の雇用者数は合計で従来推計を６万人下回った。過去３カ月間の雇用増加数は月平均５万１０００人増で、２０２５年の同時期の２万３０００人を上回った。

エコノミストは、今回の統計が労働市場の「採用も解雇も少ない」状態を改めて示したと指摘。インフレが最大の焦点となる中、目先の金融政策には影響しない可能性が高いとの見方を示した。

フィッチ・レーティングスの米経済責任者、オル・ソノラ氏は「失望を誘う雇用統計であり、採用も解雇も少ない労働市場が続いていたことを再認識させる内容だ」と指摘。「雇用の伸び悩み、失業率の小幅上昇、抑制された賃金の伸び、過去の雇用者数の下方改定を踏まえると、ＦＲＢが１０月の利上げを選択肢に残す理由はほとんどない。ただ、引き続き最も重要な統計は消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）だ」と述べた。

９月の低調な伸びと８月分の下方改定は、政府が季節的な変動を取り除くために用いる季節調整モデルに関連する変動が原因とみられる。エコノミストは、今年のようにレーバーデーの祝日が例年より遅めのときは、雇用の伸びが低調になる傾向があると指摘した。人員削減が広範に増加している兆候はない。企業利益の堅調な伸びと底堅い国内需要を背景に、新規失業保険申請件数は５７年ぶりの低水準で推移している。

ただエコノミストは、エネルギー価格の高騰や供給網の逼迫など、米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争に伴う逆風が強まり、２６年末から２７年にかけて労働市場に支障が生じ始めると予想した。

＜医療部門の雇用、小幅増にとどまる＞

医療部門は引き続き雇用増の大半を占め、１万７０００人増加した。ただ、過去１２カ月の月平均増加数３万３０００人を大きく下回った。外来医療サービスと病院で雇用が増加した一方、看護・居住型介護施設では９０００人減少した。ハイチ出身の移民数十万人を対象とする一時保護資格（ＴＰＳ）の終了が関係している可能性がある。

建設業は１万１０００人増、製造業は９０００人増だった。情報関連業は１万人、金融業は７０００人、それぞれ減少した。専門・ビジネスサービス業は人材派遣業の１万０９００人減を受けて９０００人減少した。一方、レジャー・接客業は１万人増。卸売業・小売業や運輸・倉庫業でも緩やかな雇用増がみられた。

雇用増を報告した業種の割合は４９．０％と８月の５７．６％から低下し、過去１１カ月で最も低い水準に落ち込んだ。

９月の雇用の伸びはほぼ止まったものの、週平均労働時間は３４．４時間で変わらなかった。

平均時給は０．１％上昇と、８月の０．３％上昇から伸びが縮小した。前年比でも３．０％上昇と、８月の３．１％上昇から鈍化した。

失業率の上昇は、労働力人口が４８万５０００人増加したことを反映した。これに伴い、労働参加率は８月の６１．６％から９月は６１．８％に上昇した。家計調査に基づく就業者数は４０万６０００人増加した。

ＢＭＯキャピタル・マーケッツのチーフ米国エコノミスト、スコット・アンダーソン氏は「今回の統計には労働市場が深刻な危機に陥っていることを示唆する要素は何もないが、労働市場の底堅さは国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）成長率ほど確固たる基盤には立っていない可能性が高い」と述べた。

ＣＭＥグループのフェドウオッチによると、金融市場が織り込む１０月２７─２８日の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ確率は当初約１３％に低下したものの、その後、約２３％と前日とほぼ同じ水準となった。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：ＡＩ信奉の誤算、米メタ　大規模リストラ縮小し「人間中心」に回帰 アングル：米雇用統計、利下げ観測復活の試金石に　ＦＲＢはなお慎重 アングル：3月米雇用統計、ＦＲＢの金利据え置きシナリオの補強要因に 焦点：ＡＩが10万人以上の雇用に影響か、米映画業界でリスキリング活況 アングル：試される米消費の持続力、物価高に政府閉鎖や雇用情勢悪化で 最終更新: 10/3(土) 3:39 ロイター

item.title: Brazil's Petrobras makes new oil discovery off Amapa state
item.description: Brazilian state-run oil company Petrobras said on Friday it had made a new oil discovery in ultra-deep waters off Amapa state, part of a region known as Equatorial Margin that it considers its most promising new oil frontier.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian state-run oil company Petrobras (PETR3.SA) said on Friday it had made a new oil discovery in ultra-deep waters off Amapa state, part of a region known as Equatorial Margin that it considers its most promising new oil frontier. According to a securities filing, an oil-bearing interval was found in the Morpho well, marking a new discovery in block FZA-M-59, where it had already [USN:S0N44906J TEXT:"identified hydrocarbons"] in August. Discovery was made in a second reservoir, deeper in the same well of the August oil discovery, according to the company Work on the well is expected to conclude by end of October, CEO Magda Chambriard told reporters on Friday Petrobras will drill [USN:L1N44W0HV TEXT:"three new wells"] in the area to determine wether commercial production in the environmentally-sensitive Foz do Amazonas basin is viable Petrobras has seven wells still to be licensed for drilling in the region, said Chambriard Foz do Amazonas shares geological similarities with offshore Guyana, where ExxonMobil (XOM.N) is developing huge fields

item.title: Nike’s struggles test investor confidence in CEO Hill’s turnaround effort
item.description: When Nike brought Elliott Hill out of retirement in October 2024, investors hoped the company veteran would quickly reverse years of product missteps, rebuild relationships with wholesalers and ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: When Nike brought Elliott Hill out of retirement in October 2024, investors hoped the company veteran would quickly reverse years of product missteps, rebuild relationships with wholesalers and restore the sportswear giant’s lost momentum. Two years on, Nike’s market value and earnings have more than halved, while many of the problems Hill was hired to fix - from weakness in China to over-reliance on discounted lifestyle products - continue to weigh on the business. The unfinished turnaround was on display again on Thursday when Nike announced another round of job cuts and forecast steeper-than-expected declines in sales and profit for the fiscal year ending in May 2028. “Things are going to get worse before they get better,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Piral Dadhania said. That timeline was reinforced by Nike’s disclosure that most of the savings from its overhaul will not be realized until fiscal 2029 and 2030. Nike on Thursday once again flagged performance in sportswear, China and its legacy Jordan brand as problem areas. Together, they accounted for more than half of total sales. Investor day in focus Nike’s turnaround challenges have become a test of investor faith in CEO Hill’s strategy ahead of its investor day on November 16 and 17, where analysts expect the company to provide a clearer roadmap for restoring growth and profitability. Hill was brought back to steady a company that had lost its footing under a strategy that prioritized direct sales and reduced ties with wholesale partners, while leaning heavily on a shrinking roster of lifestyle products instead of its core sports strategy. Since returning, he has moved to rebuild relationships with retailers, refocus product development on sports and simplify operations. Yet revenue continues to decline across wholesale and direct channels. “Nike really needs to show that it can at least bail out problems faster than taking them on,” said Neil Saunders managing director of GlobalData. “The job cuts and associated cost-cutting will buy time and may support margins and the bottom line - but these things are not the solution to the brand problems that are the cause of decline,” he said. Shares were down about 10 per cent in premarket trading on Friday. They were trading at about US$31.58, their lowest in 12 years and far behind a 2021 peak of about $175. The challenges are more evident in China, once one of Nike’s most important growth engines but now a problem area. Hill acknowledged on Thursday that efforts to stabilize the market will take “multiple seasons” and will weigh on profitability. “With the November analyst day ahead, we would assume management likely preferred to get the ‘bad news’ out of the way to offer up a more positive tone in person, but clearly there has been plenty of ‘bad news’ to spare,” said Simeon Siegel, analyst at Guggenheim. The Jordan brand offered another illustration of the work that remains. Nike is trying to return the franchise to premium growth by reducing the number and frequency of retro sneaker launches after years of oversupply and discounting. “Simply put we’ve been oversupplying our iconic retro product, asking them to do too much,” Hill said. He admitted that a “lack of energy in the lifestyle space” was hurting traffic, but said it was up to Nike as the industry’s leader to bring back more innovation and creativity to the category. “Good thing Nike excels in running shoes because they continue to have an uphill climb ahead of them,” said Greg Zakowicz, e-commerce and retail advisor at online marketing firm Omnisend. “Its plan may be more challenging than first expected.” (Reporting by Juveria Tabassum and Angela Christy in Bengaluru; Editing by Lisa Jucca and Arun Koyyur)

item.title: US halts consular services in Brazil ahead of election, increasing tensions
item.description: Citing security concerns, the United States suspended consular services on Friday, prompting Australia to also close its embassy two days before the country's presidential election, fueling an already uneasy environment ahead of the high-stakes vote.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu, Doina Chiacu
item.content:encoded: Citing security concerns, the United States suspended consular services on Friday, prompting Australia to also close its embassy two days before the country's presidential election, fueling an already uneasy environment ahead of the high-stakes vote. Brazil's Federal Police said on Friday afternoon they had carried out preventive searches in Sao Paulo and near Brasilia, but had so far found no evidence of a threat or identified any suspects linked to criminal organizations. The State Department did not elaborate on the security issues or link them to Sunday's election, which has been marked by tensions over alleged foreign interference and strains between Washington and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's government. "We are working closely with our Brazilian counterparts to address the security concerns," a department spokesperson said in an email. The department did not say when the consular services would resume. "Consular Services in the US Embassy and Consulates in Brazil will be suspended starting Friday, October 2 due to security concerns," it said in a statement Thursday. "US citizens seeking emergency assistance during this time should not come to the Embassy, the Consulates, or other US diplomatic facilities." Australia's ambassador to Brazil, Sophie Davies, said on social media that the Australian embassy in Brasilia would also be closed on Friday due to security concerns, citing the alert issued by the US and advising Australians to avoid US embassies and consulates in Brazil. Brazil's foreign ministry declined to comment on the matter. ELECTION TENSIONS The State Department made the announcement at a tense moment for US-Brazil relations. Brazilians will [USN:L6N45K0PD TEXT:"vote"] for president on Sunday in a race that will determine whether Latin America's largest nation follows the conservative shift that US President Donald Trump has often cheered on from Washington. Lula and his allies [USN:S0N44O041 TEXT:"have warned"] of foreign interference in the election, pointing to [USN:FWN43H1K7 TEXT:"tariffs"] and [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"an effort"] by Washington to send officials to Brazil to "discuss electoral integrity." Edinho Silva, president of Lula's Workers' Party, called Friday's closures "unprecedented" in a press conference. "It makes no sense at all. It's one of Trump's ways of trying to influence Brazilian public opinion," Silva said. Though he has publicly praised Lula's main right-wing opponent Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, and the State Department has rejected claims of election meddling, but the issue has hovered over the race. Brazilian intelligence officials this month briefed a French and German delegation in Brasilia on what they [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"described as US and Russian interference"] before Brazil's election. The visit underlined growing concern on both sides of the Atlantic over Trump's efforts to support like-minded candidates. Violent crime has also dominated the list of voter concerns in Brazilian election polls, prompting candidates to pledge tougher security measures.

FAST

Oct 2 : Standard Chartered expects the European Central Bank to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.75 per cent in December, reversing its previous call for a pause, after stronger-than-expected inflation and resilient economic activity reinforced the case for further tightening. The brokerage changed its forecast after euro zone inflation accelerated more than expected in September, driven largely by higher energy prices, while recent business activity data pointed to a more resilient economy than previously anticipated. Major Wall Street banks have broadly coalesced around expectations for another ECB rate hike in December. ECB, along with several other major central banks, raised interest rates last month as policymakers sought to contain inflation risks stemming from higher energy costs and resilient economic growth.

"We think the ECB will opt to take rates slightly into restrictive territory," the brokerage's economists wrote in a note, adding that policymakers may seek insurance against the risk of higher energy prices feeding through to wages and broader price pressures. The ECB will next meet on October 29, but Standard Chartered said a December rate hike is more likely, as policymakers will then have updated economic forecasts and another round of inflation data, despite limited signs of second-round price pressures. Money markets are pricing in a roughly 65 per cent probability that the ECB will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, LSEG data showed.
